paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: For this part, you are allowed 30 minutes to write an essay that begins with the sentence “In an era of information explosion, it is vitally important to develop the ability to think critically and make rational choices.” You can make statements, give reasons, or cite examples to develop your essay. You should write at least 150 words but no more than 200 words.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：对于这一部分，你有30分钟的时间写一篇文章，开头是“在信息爆炸的时代，培养批判性思维和做出理性选择的能力至关重要。”你可以发表陈述、给出理由或引用例子来展开你的论文。你应该写至少150字但不超过200字。

paragraphs.sourceText: The task of the global strategist of a business is to build a platform of capabilities derived from the resources, experiences and innovations of units operating in multiple locations, to transplant those capabilities wherever 26 , and then to systematically upgrade and renew them — ahead of the competition.
paragraphs.translationZh: 企业全球战略家的任务是建立一个源自多个地点运营单位的资源、经验和创新的能力平台，将这些能力移植到适当的地方，然后系统地升级和更新它们——领先于竞争对手。

paragraphs.sourceText: Apple is an outstanding case of a company whose unique capabilities give it a worldwide 27 advantage, particularly with respect to its ability to build platforms from a product base that integrates functional and 28 design. Apple has been able to leverage and exploit its California-based design and marketing advantages successfully throughout the world. IKEA is another such case. The do-it-yourself furniture and houseware company first developed a compelling set of capabilities to design, manufacture and 29 furniture at low cost and sell it in a novel way in Sweden. Later, IKEA successfully 30 this formula in many other countries.
paragraphs.translationZh: 苹果公司是一个杰出的案例，它的独特能力赋予了它全球竞争优势，特别是它能够从集成功能和美学设计的产品基础上构建平台。苹果已经能够在全球范围内成功地利用和利用其位于加州的设计和营销优势。宜家是另一个这样的案例。这家DIY家具和家居用品公司首先开发了一套引人注目的能力，以低成本设计、制造和运输家具，并以新颖的方式在瑞典销售。后来，宜家在许多其他国家成功复制了这一公式。

paragraphs.sourceText: By contrast, Telefónica, a Spanish telecommunications company that is now the world’s fifth largest telecom by 31 , first developed its special advantage abroad. In 1989 and 1990, Telefónica had the opportunity to enter Chile and Argentina, countries that shared many institutional and cultural characteristics with its home country but that were 32 more rapid market reform. Throughout the 1990s, Telefónica took what it learned in Chile and Argentina about reconstructing former state-owned telecoms to other Latin American countries that were privatizing their state telecoms and deregulating their telecom markets.
paragraphs.translationZh: 相比之下，西班牙电信公司 Telefónica（按收入计算，目前已成为全球第五大电信公司）首先在国外发展了其特殊优势。 1989年和1990年，西班牙电信有机会进入智利和阿根廷，这两个国家与其母国有许多共同的制度和文化特征，但正在经历更快的市场改革。整个 90 年代，Telefónica 将其在智利和阿根廷重建前国有电信公司的经验带到了其他正在将国有电信私有化并放松电信市场管制的拉丁美洲国家。

paragraphs.sourceText: These examples might lead the reader to believe that creating a global advantage is an easy task. But many other 33 of expensive failed experiments suggest that creating a lasting global advantage actually requires a great deal of 34 and operational finesse (技巧). Our research suggests that global winners typically create and sustain their international presence through a systematic process of 35 , renewing and enhancing their core capabilities.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这些例子可能会让读者相信创造全球优势是一件容易的事。但许多其他昂贵的失败实验实例表明，创造持久的全球优势实际上需要大量的战略和运营技巧。我们的研究表明，全球赢家通常通过开发、更新和增强其核心能力的系统过程来创建和维持其国际影响力。

paragraphs.sourceText: Directions: In this section, you are going to read a passage with ten statements attached to it. Each statement contains information given in one of the paragraphs. Identify the paragraph from which the information is derived. You may choose a paragraph more than once. Each paragraph is marked with a letter. Answer the questions by marking the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：在本节中，您将阅读一段附有十个陈述的段落。每条陈述都包含其中一个段落中给出的信息。确定信息来源的段落。您可以多次选择一个段落。每个段落都标有一个字母。通过在答题卡 2 上标记相应的字母来回答问题。

paragraphs.sourceText: Fear of Nature: An Emerging Threat to Conservation
paragraphs.translationZh: 对自然的恐惧：对自然保护的新威胁

paragraphs.sourceText: A) What do we lose when natural spaces and species disappear? Increasingly, research has shown that as species and ecosystems vanish, it also chips away at our ability to preserve what remains — because we no longer understand what we’re losing.
paragraphs.translationZh: A）当自然空间和物种消失时，我们会失去什么？越来越多的研究表明，随着物种和生态系统的消失，我们保护剩余物种的能力也随之减弱——因为我们不再了解我们正在失去什么。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) You probably see it all the time. The neighbor who puts pesticides on his lawn rather than deal with annoying bees. The politician who votes against wildlife protection because she’s never seen a wolf in the wild. The corporation that wants to bulldoze (用推土机推平) the habitat of a rare frog.
paragraphs.translationZh: B) 你可能经常看到它。邻居在他的草坪上喷洒杀虫剂，而不是对付烦人的蜜蜂。投票反对野生动物保护的政客，因为她从未在野外见过狼。该公司想要推土机推平稀有青蛙的栖息地。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) At best this can be termed “the extinction of experience.” where our cultural and natural histories fade from our memories and therefore our reality. At its worst it becomes something even more concerning: “biophobia,” the fear of living things and a complete aversion to nature.
paragraphs.translationZh: C）这充其量可以被称为“经验的消失”。在那里，我们的文化和自然历史从我们的记忆中消失，从而从我们的现实中消失。在最坏的情况下，它会变得更加令人担忧：“生物恐惧症”，即对生物的恐惧和对自然的完全厌恶。

paragraphs.sourceText: D) This isn’t the fiction of living in a cold, empty dystopia (绝望的世界). Sadly, it’s becoming a way of life for too many people — especially children. A recent study in Japan paints a striking portrait of this problem. A survey of more than 5,300 school children in the Tochigi Prefecture examined their perception of 14 local insect species and one spider. The results? A collective “ew!” Most of the students saw the species as things to dislike or fear, or even as sources of danger. The less experience the students had with nature, the more negative their feelings.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 这并不是生活在寒冷、空虚的反乌托邦（绝望的世界）中的小说。可悲的是，它正在成为太多人——尤其是儿童——的一种生活方式。日本最近的一项研究描绘了这个问题的惊人景象。对栃木县 5,300 多名学童进行的一项调查调查了他们对 14 种当地昆虫和一种蜘蛛的看法。结果？集体“哎哟！”大多数学生认为该物种是令人厌恶或恐惧的事物，甚至是危险的来源。学生对自然的体验越少，他们的感受就越消极。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The results were published earlier this year in the journal Biological Conservation. Lead researcher Masashi Soga with the University of Tokyo says the study stemmed from observations about today’s nature-deficient children. “Humans inherently avoid dangerous organisms such as bees, but children these days avoid even harmless animals such as butterflies and dragonflies (蜻蜓).” he says. “I have long wondered why so many of today’s children react like this.”
paragraphs.translationZh: E) 研究结果于今年早些时候发表在《生物保护》杂志上。东京大学首席研究员 Masashi Soga 表示，这项研究源于对当今缺乏天性的儿童的观察。 “人类天生会避开蜜蜂等危险生物，但现在的孩子们甚至会避开蝴蝶和蜻蜓等无害动物。”他说。 “我一直想知道为什么现在有这么多孩子会有这样的反应。”

paragraphs.sourceText: F) Although the children’s reactions were somewhat expected, the new study did contain an unexpected finding: Many of the surveyed children revealed that their parents also expressed fear or disgust of the same animals. In fact these parental emotions were strong enough to overwhelm any positive experiences the children might have gained from direct experiences in nature. As Soga and his coauthors wrote in their paper, “Our results suggest that there is likely a feedback loop in which an increase in people who have negative attitudes towards nature in one generation will lead to a further increase in people with similar attitudes in the next generation.”
paragraphs.translationZh: F) 虽然孩子们的反应在某种程度上是意料之中的，但新研究确实有一个意想不到的发现：许多接受调查的孩子透露，他们的父母也对同一种动物表达了恐惧或厌恶。事实上，这些父母的情绪强烈到足以压倒孩子们可能从大自然的直接经历中获得的任何积极经历。正如苏我和他的合著者在他们的论文中所写的那样，“我们的研究结果表明，可能存在一个反馈循环，在这一循环中，一代人对自然持消极态度的人数增加，将导致下一代持有类似态度的人进一步增加。”

paragraphs.sourceText: G) And that’s possibly the greater threat posed by extinction of experience. Soga suggests the generational loss — a condition previously dubbed environmental generational amnesia (遗忘) — could chip away at our societal ability to preserve what we’re losing. “I believe that increased biophobia is a major, but invisible, threat to global biodiversity,” Soga says. “As the number of children who have biophobia increases, public interest and support for biodiversity conservation will gradually decline. Although many conservation biologists still consider that preventing the loss of wildlife habitat is the most important way to conserve biodiversity, I think preventing increased biophobia is also important for conservation.”
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 这可能是经验消失带来的更大威胁。索加认为，代际损失——一种以前被称为环境代际失忆症（遗忘症）的疾病——可能会削弱我们社会保护我们正在失去的东西的能力。 “我认为，越来越多的生物恐惧症对全球生物多样性构成了重大但无形的威胁，”索加说。 “随着患有生物恐惧症的儿童数量增加，公众对生物多样性保护的兴趣和支持将逐渐下降。尽管许多保护生物学家仍然认为防止野生动物栖息地丧失是保护生物多样性的最重要方法，但我认为防止生物恐惧症增加对于保护也很重要。”

paragraphs.sourceText: H) What’s to be done about this? The paper makes several recommendations, the most obvious of which is that children should experience nature more often. The authors also suggest establishing policies to guide these natural experiences and increasing educational programs about the natural world.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 对此该怎么办？该论文提出了几项建议，其中最明显的是孩子应该更多地体验大自然。作者还建议制定政策来指导这些自然体验，并增加有关自然世界的教育项目。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) Helping parents to see species around them in a new light would make a difference, too. And, of course, maintaining support for preserving the wild spaces where these “scary” creatures live is the most important thing of all. That’s a point reinforced by another recent study, which found that wild spaces located within urban areas — and the plants and animals that thrive in them — are particularly important for human health and well-being.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 帮助父母以新的眼光看待周围的物种也会产生影响。当然，维持对保护这些“可怕”生物居住的野生空间的支持是最重要的事情。最近的另一项研究也证实了这一点，该研究发现城市地区的野生空间以及在其中繁衍生息的植物和动物对于人类的健康和福祉尤其重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) Published in the journal Frontiers in Sustainable Cities, the study examined attitudes toward Discovery Park, the heavily forested 534-acre public park in Seattle, Washington. It found that the public had the most appreciation for — and gained the most value from — the wildest parts of the park. “I have seen whales, seals, fish, eagles, shorebirds and many other sea creatures in their natural habitat,” one survey participant wrote. “Coming here with people has allowed me to connect and talk with them about conversation that simply does not happen in everyday life.” wrote another.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 该研究发表在《可持续城市前沿》杂志上，调查了人们对探索公园的态度，该公园位于华盛顿州西雅图，占地 534 英亩，森林茂密。研究发现，公众最欣赏公园最狂野的部分，并从中获得最大的价值。 “我在自然栖息地看到了鲸鱼、海豹、鱼类、鹰、滨鸟和许多其他海洋生物，”一位调查参与者写道。 “和人们一起来到这里让我能够与他们联系并谈论日常生活中根本不会发生的对话。”又写了一篇。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The participants reported that their most valuable experiences in the park included encountering wildlife, walking through open spaces, exploring the beach and finding beautiful views. “We saw that a large majority of participants’ interactions, especially their most meaningful interactions, depended on Discovery Park’s relative wildness,” says lead author Elizabeth Lev, a master’s student in the University of Washington’s Human Interaction with Nature Lab. This is only possible because the park is relatively wild. After all, you can’t enjoy watching birds if there are no birds to follow; gaze at the sunset if it’s obscured by skyscrapers; or stop and smell the flowers if they don’t have room to grow.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 参与者报告说，他们在公园里最有价值的经历包括遇到野生动物、穿过开放空间、探索海滩和发现美丽的景色。 “我们发现，绝大多数参与者的互动，尤其是他们最有意义的互动，都取决于探索公园的相对野性，”主要作者、华盛顿大学人类与自然互动实验室的硕士生伊丽莎白·列夫 (Elizabeth Lev) 说道。这是可能的，因为公园相对比较荒凉。毕竟，如果没有鸟可跟随，你就无法享受观鸟的乐趣；如果日落被摩天大楼遮挡，可以凝视日落；或者如果花没有空间生长，就停下来闻闻花香。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) And yet even this long-protected space could someday become less hospitable to nature. Over the past few years a lot of people and organizations have suggested developing parts of Discovery Park or the neighboring area. Most recently a plan proposed building 34 acres of much-needed affordable housing and parking spaces adjacent to the park, bringing with them noise, traffic and pollution.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 然而，即使是这个长期受到保护的空间也可能有一天变得不那么适合大自然。过去几年，许多人和组织建议开发探索公园或邻近地区的部分地区。最近的一项计划提议在公园附近建造 34 英亩急需的经济适用住房和停车位，但随之而来的是噪音、交通和污染。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) If anything like that happened, both the park and the people of Seattle could lose something vital. And that would continue the trend of chipping away at Seattle’s — and the world’s — natural spaces leaving just tiny pocket parks and green-but-empty spaces that offer little real value to wildlife, plants or people.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 如果发生类似的事情，公园和西雅图人民都可能会失去一些重要的东西。这将继续侵蚀西雅图乃至世界自然空间的趋势，只留下小公园和绿色但空旷的空间，对野生动物、植物或人类几乎没有真正的价值。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) “It is true that any interaction with nature is better than none, but I don’t want people to be satisfied with any small bit of grass and trees,” Lev says. “We have been in this cycle of environmental generational amnesia for a long time, where the baseline keeps shifting and we don’t even realize what we’re losing until it’s gone. If we can get people to understand how much meaning and value can come from having more experiences with more wild forms of nature, then maybe we can stop this cycle and move toward conserving and restoring what we have left.”
paragraphs.translationZh: N）“确实，与自然的任何互动都比没有好，但我不希望人们对任何一小片草和树感到满意，”列夫说。 “我们已经处于这种环境代际失忆症的循环中很长一段时间了，基线不断变化，直到它消失之前我们甚至没有意识到我们正在失去什么。如果我们能让人们了解更多的体验更多的野生自然形式可以带来多大的意义和价值，那么也许我们可以停止这个循环，并转向保护和恢复我们剩下的东西。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O) Building this understanding in an ever-more fearful and disconnected world may be the biggest challenge. Peter Kahn, the senior author of Lev’s paper and the director of the Human Interaction with Nature lab, made several suggestions for bridging this gap in this 2011 book, Technological Nature. They echo the recommendation about getting children into nature, but also include telling stories of how things used to be, imagining what things might be like in the future, and developing a common language about nature, “a way of speaking about wild and domestic interaction patterns, and the meaningful, deep and often joyful feelings that they generate.” P. No matter what techniques we use, this growing field of research illustrates that saving nature requires encouraging people to experience it more often and more deeply. That calls for additional research — Lev and her coauthors have published a toolkit that other municipalities can follow to study the value of their own wild spaces — and clear communication of the results. “If we can continue to show people the benefits of these wild spaces,” Lev says, “maybe people will begin to see more value in keeping these areas undeveloped — for the sake of our mutual benefit.”
paragraphs.translationZh: O) 在一个更加恐惧和孤立的世界中建立这种理解可能是最大的挑战。 Lev 论文的资深作者、人类与自然互动实验室主任 Peter Kahn 在 2011 年出版的《技术自然》一书中提出了一些弥合这一差距的建议。他们回应了让孩子们融入大自然的建议，但也包括讲述事物过去的样子，想象未来的事物会是什么样子，并发展一种关于自然的共同语言，“一种谈论野生和家庭互动模式，以及它们所产生的有意义、深刻且常常令人愉悦的感受的方式。” P. 无论我们使用什么技术，这个不断发展的研究领域表明，拯救自然需要鼓励人们更频繁、更深入地体验它。这就需要进行更多的研究——列夫和她的合著者已经发布了一个工具包，其他城市可以遵循这个工具包来研究自己的野生空间的价值——并清楚地传达结果。 “如果我们能够继续向人们展示这些野生空间的好处，”列夫说，“也许人们会开始看到保持这些地区未开发的更多价值——为了我们的共同利益。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36. A new study found parents’ aversion to certain animals would pass on to their children.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36. 一项新的研究发现，父母对某些动物的厌恶会遗传给他们的孩子。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37. The disappearance of species and ecological systems erodes our ability to keep what is left.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some people in the US have asserted that forgiving student loan debt is one way to stimulate the economy and give assistance to those in need. One government proposition is to eliminate $10,000 of debt for ‘economically distressed’ students. Some in US Congress have gone so far as to suggest forgiving up to $50,000 in debt per student borrower, but does forgiving student debt necessarily correlate to helping the economically disadvantaged?
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国一些人士声称，免除学生贷款债务是刺激经济、向有需要的人提供援助的一种方式。政府的一项提议是消除“经济困难”学生 10,000 美元的债务。美国国会的一些人甚至建议免除每个学生借款人高达 50,000 美元的债务，但免除学生债务是否一定与帮助经济弱势群体相关？

paragraphs.sourceText: The answer is no. This policy is just giving money away to universities and the most affluent students in attendance. Federal Reserve data reveals that the highest-income 40 percent of households owe approximately 60 percent of outstanding student debt, while the lowest 40 percent owe just under 20 percent. This could be due to a combination of factors: students from high-income households are more likely to go to expensive colleges, less likely to receive financial aid, and more likely to have high incomes post-graduation. Plus, the majority of student debt is held by graduate degree earners, who earn approximately 25 percent more than their undergraduate counterparts. Clearly, giving free reign to banks to forgive student debt is a step in the wrong direction.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答案是否定的。这项政策只是把钱捐给大学和最富裕的学生。美联储数据显示，收入最高的 40% 家庭欠下了大约 60% 的未偿还学生债务，而收入最低的 40% 家庭则欠下不到 20%。这可能是多种因素造成的：来自高收入家庭的学生更有可能进入昂贵的大学，获得经济援助的可能性较小，毕业后更有可能获得高收入。此外，大部分学生债务由研究生学位获得者承担，他们的收入比本科生高出约 25%。显然，让银行自由地免除学生债务是朝着错误方向迈出的一步。

paragraphs.sourceText: Other proposals for broader, long-term student loan plans have some fundamental problems. One idea is to cancel student debt only for undergraduate degrees and for students making less than $125,000.
paragraphs.translationZh: 其他更广泛、长期的学生贷款计划的提案也存在一些根本性问题。一种想法是仅取消本科学位和收入低于 125,000 美元的学生的学生债务。

paragraphs.sourceText: This attempts to address the fact that Congress’ previously mentioned student loan forgiveness plan largely helps out the wealthy, but is an adverse incentive for universities to keep raising tuition and for students to choose to major in low-earning degree programs. Colleges have no reason to make their programs more affordable if they believe students will just take out more debt. And, students will feel more comfortable making the irresponsible decision to go tens of thousands of dollars in debt to major in impractical or idealistic subjects if they know their loans will be forgiven.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这试图解决这样一个事实：国会之前提到的学生贷款减免计划在很大程度上帮助了富人，但却对大学继续提高学费和学生选择低收入学位课程产生了不利的激励。如果大学相信学生只会承担更多的债务，那么他们就没有理由让他们的课程变得更加负担得起。而且，如果学生知道自己的贷款会被免除，他们会更放心地做出不负责任的决定，背负数万美元的债务去主修不切实际或理想主义的科目。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is especially concerning given the pandemic (大流行病) has rendered a college education practically worthless. Students are paying tens of thousands of dollars per year to live at home and be lectured on the Internet. Do we really want to tell colleges that they can get away with providing below-average service for an outrageous cost?
paragraphs.translationZh: 鉴于大流行病使大学教育几乎毫无价值，这一点尤其令人担忧。学生每年要支付数万美元才能住在家里并在互联网上接受授课。我们真的想告诉大学，他们可以以高得离谱的成本提供低于平均水平的服务吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: In the case of any of these student debt plans, working-class Americans who chose not to or could not afford to go to college will be subsidizing the education of the professional class. Plumbers and retail workers will be paying for the degrees of doctors and lawyers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在任何这些学生债务计划的情况下，选择不或无力上大学的美国工薪阶层都将补贴专业阶层的教育。水管工和零售工人将支付医生和律师学位的费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: The Us government’s effort to help those in debt is commendable but is this really the solution that will help the poor financially recover?
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国政府帮助债务人的努力值得称赞，但这真的能帮助穷人恢复经济吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: If there’s one rule that most parents cling to in the confusing, fast-changing world of kids and media, it’s “No screens before age 2.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果说在这个令人困惑、瞬息万变的儿童和媒体世界中，大多数父母都遵守一条规则的话，那就是“两岁之前不要看电子屏幕”。

paragraphs.sourceText: As of today, that rule has been thrown out the window. The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), which first issued that recommendation back in 1999, has extensively updated and revised its guidelines for children and adolescents to reflect new research and new habits.
paragraphs.translationZh: 截至今天，这条规则已被抛到了九霄云外。美国儿科学会 (AAP) 于 1999 年首次发布该建议，并广泛更新和修订了其针对儿童和青少年的指南，以反映新的研究和新的习惯。

paragraphs.sourceText: The new guidelines, especially for very young children, shift the focus from WHAT is on the screen to WHO else is in the room. And in doing so, they raise some intriguing points about the future of learning from media.
paragraphs.translationZh: 新的指南，特别是针对年幼的儿童，将焦点从屏幕上的内容转移到房间里的其他人。在此过程中，他们对媒体学习的未来提出了一些有趣的观点。

paragraphs.sourceText: For babies younger than 18 months, AAP still says no screens at all are the best idea — with one notable exception: Live video chat. Surveys indicate that families already popularly believe that “Face time doesn’t count”, or at least that the benefit of virtual visits with grandparents or other relatives outweighs the potential cost of exposing babies to the laptop or smartphone.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于 18 个月以下的婴儿，AAP 仍然表示最好不要使用屏幕，但有一个明显的例外：实时视频聊天。调查显示，家庭已经普遍认为“面对面的时间不算数”，或者至少认为与祖父母或其他亲戚进行虚拟拜访的好处超过了让婴儿接触笔记本电脑或智能手机的潜在成本。

paragraphs.sourceText: The AAP doesn’t cite positive evidence that infants actually get something out of this kind of “conversation”, the way that they clearly do from live social interaction. But there’s some observational research that infants as young as six months old are emotionally engaged by playing live peekaboo (躲猫猫游戏) with Grandma online.
paragraphs.translationZh: 美国儿科学会并没有引用积极的证据来证明婴儿确实能从这种“对话”中得到一些东西，而他们显然是从实时社交互动中得到的。但有一些观察性研究表明，六个月大的婴儿会通过在网上和奶奶玩躲猫猫游戏来进行情感投入。

paragraphs.sourceText: For infants and toddlers (学步儿童), ages 15 months to 2 years old, there’s limited evidence from a couple of very small studies that they can learn new words from educational media, if and only if parents are watching alongside them, repeating what the video says and/or drawing attention to what is on the screen. In other words, treating a video or an app like a picture book is the best bet.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于学步儿童（15 个月至 2 岁），几项小型研究的有限证据表明，当且仅当父母在他们旁边观看、重复视频内容和/或吸引人们注意屏幕上的内容时，他们才能从教育媒体中学习新单词。换句话说，将视频或应用程序视为图画书是最好的选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: The flip side of this is that many studies have actually shown poorer language skills correlated with earlier solo viewing of “educational” videos. There’s also research that shows language delays in children who watch more TV and start watching earlier. In both cases, the problem seems to be media replacing interaction with people. For this reason, the new AAP guideline has changed from “avoid all screens under age 2” to “avoid solo media use in this age group.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 另一方面，许多研究实际上表明，较早单独观看“教育”视频的语言能力较差。还有研究表明，看电视越多、开始看电视的时间越早，孩子的语言能力就越迟缓。在这两种情况下，问题似乎都是媒体取代了人与人之间的互动。因此，新的 AAP 指南已从“避免 2 岁以下的所有屏幕”更改为“避免该年龄组单独使用媒体”。

paragraphs.sourceText: For preschoolers ages 2 to 5, there’s more evidence that they have the ability to transfer knowledge from screens to the real world, including early literacy and math. For this age group, AAP recommends no more than an hour a day of screen use. And, just as with younger children, they want care-givers to take part in screen time: “Co-view with your children, help children understand what they are seeing, and help them apply what they learn to the world around them.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于 2 至 5 岁的学龄前儿童，有更多证据表明他们有能力将知识从屏幕转移到现实世界，包括早期识字和数学。对于这个年龄段的人，美国儿科学会建议每天使用屏幕的时间不要超过一个小时。而且，就像年幼的孩子一样，他们希望看护者参与屏幕时间：“与孩子共同观看，帮助孩子理解他们所看到的内容，并帮助他们将学到的知识应用到周围的世界。”

paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 关于“2岁以下禁止放映”规则，我们了解到什么？

paragraphs.translationZh: 55. 作者对 2 至 5 岁的学龄前儿童有何看法？
